processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Moulds 32 mm in diameter by 186 mm in length; as-cast terminal state (no further heat treatment reported).
Samples cut from cast ingots by spark erosion in the direction of the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction); specimen surfaces ground.

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase Fe3Al matrix with MC carbide (VC) precipitates

phase_interfaces.coherence: (001) matrix planes parallel to (001) precipitate planes (orientation relationship)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Relatively thin (about 0.5 mm as printed in b0029; Table 1 gives 0.5 μm) and sharp plate-like VC precipitates cause notch sensitivity of the matrix and a pronounced tension–compression asymmetry (≈36%).

interfaces.slip_behavior: Screw dislocation glide with nonplanar (delocalised) core structure contributes to the tension–compression asymmetry.
interfaces.phase_evolution: D03/B2 order–disorder transition at around 550 °C; B2/A2 at around 800 °C before melting.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression: (6×6×10) mm^3; tension: flat (3.5×5) mm^2 cross-section with 15 mm gauge length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Specimens cut along the longitudinal axis (casting direction); surfaces ground; ZWICK 1474 universal testing machine.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression (6×6×10) mm^3; tension flat (3.5×5) mm^2 cross-section, 15 mm gauge length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Elevated-temperature tests in radiation furnace; samples held 30 min at testing temperature before loading; temperature checked by NiCr–Ni thermocouple on the specimen surface.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: load of 62.5 g (as printed) with an indentation ball of 2.5 mm diameter
characterization_methods.key_findings: Matrix hardness of Fe-26Al-2V-1C is 286 HB.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; compression samples (6×6×10) mm^3; tensile flat samples (3.5×5) mm^2 cross-section, 15 mm gauge length; specimens cut along casting direction and ground; elevated-temperature tests in protective argon within a radiation furnace.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine yield stress in compression/tension and total elongation at room and elevated temperatures.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Room temperature: compression yield 544 MPa, tension yield 350 MPa, elongation 0.5%; pronounced tension–compression asymmetry ≈36%. Elevated temperature: yield stress anomaly peak at about 550 °C with about 400 MPa; tension–compression asymmetry at 650 and 800 °C.

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with secondary electrons (SE)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-Hitachi S-530, 20 kV, working distance 15 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe fracture mode after tensile testing
characterization_methods.key_findings: Uniform step-like transgranular fracture (TGC) with plate-like (needle-shaped) VC precipitates; fracture facets formed on (001) matrix planes parallel to (001) precipitate planes.

unmapped_findings: At 650 °C and 800 °C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C exhibits tension–compression asymmetry (compression yield stress > tension yield stress); no numeric value labels are printed for individual bars in Fig. 7/Fig. 8 [b0040][figure_007][figure_008].

In b0029 the VC precipitate thickness is printed as 'about 0.5 mm', while Table 1 lists the VC size as 0.5×15 μm; the precipitates are described as thin and sharp plate-like and cause notch sensitivity of the matrix [b0029][b0015].

Room-temperature compression stress–strain curve of Fe-26Al-2V-1C (curve 9, Fig. 2b) shows nearly constant hardening rate over long strain intervals before a final parabolic stage [b0027][figure_002].
